description:
Sheet 2 of 5 of Drawing S-401.0 (City of Los Angeles Department of Transportation). Heading: MAJOR HIGHWAYS (prior to 11-10-99), 100' R/W - 80' roadway. Two plan views of a 100-foot right-of-way with an 80-foot roadway, each with a 10' strip outside each curb, shown from mid-block on the left to an intersection with a signal-controlled cross street on the right (circled S). Both views have a double yellow center line with a left turn lane and a STOPPING PROHIBITION arrow along the curb below the view, running the length of the block.

Upper plan view, no bike lanes: Overall dimensions are 100' right-of-way, 80' roadway and 40' from the center line to each curb. At mid-block the center two-way left turn lane is 10' to 12' wide with 11' lanes on each side and 23' to 24' from the center turn lane edge to the curb on each side (dimension strings read 23' to 24', 11', 10' to 12', 11'). Lane lines are broken. A critical driveway (box with X) at the lower left has a 70' MIN. dimension beside it. On the right, a 12" YELLOW TAPER of 100' TO 120' transitions the two-way left turn lane into a two-lane left turn pocket (two left turn arrows) at the intersection. A callout labels the 12" yellow line along the taper and a 12' dimension appears at the taper end. At the intersection the dimension strings read 19', 11', 10', 10', 11', 19' across the 80' roadway.

Lower plan view, with bike lanes: Same 100' R/W, 80' roadway (40' each side), 10' outside strips. A bike lane (NOTE 9) is drawn along each curb with 5' lane and 8' parking or curb width dimensions: strings read 8', 5', 11', 11', 10', 11', 11', 5', 8'. The lower bike lane line is drawn in two lengths. A critical driveway with a 30' MIN. dimension is at the lower left. On the right a single left turn pocket is set off from the center two-way left turn lane by a reverse curve taper labeled 60' OR 80' with a left turn arrow. Intersection strings read 8', 5', 11', 11', 10', 11', 11', 13'. Title block: TYPICAL MAJOR HIGHWAY STRIPING TREATMENTS, Drawing No. S-401.0, sheet 2 of 5.
notes: No numbered notes appear on this sheet. The sheet refers to Note 9 for the bike lane (the note text is on sheet 1 of this drawing). Callouts on the sheet: 12" YELLOW TAPER, 100' TO 120' TAPER, CRITICAL DRIVEWAY, 70' MIN., 30' MIN., 60' OR 80', BIKE LANE (NOTE 9), STOPPING PROHIBITION.
title: Typical Major Highway Striping Treatments (100' R/W - 80' Roadway, Prior to 11-10-99), Sheet 2 of 5
summary: Two plan views of a 100-foot right-of-way major highway with an 80-foot roadway, one without bike lanes and one with 5-foot bike lanes. Each shows a two-way left turn lane that tapers (100' to 120' taper, or 60' or 80' reverse curve) into a left turn pocket at a signalized intersection. Critical driveways must be 70' (no bike lanes) or 30' (bike lanes) minimum from the transition, and the curb stopping prohibition runs the full block.

description:
Sheet 3 of 5 of Drawing S-401.0. Heading: MAJOR HIGHWAYS (prior to 11-10-99), 100' R/W - 80' roadway. Three plan views of raised median treatments, each running from mid-block on the left to a signalized intersection on the right (circled S). Each has STOPPING PROHIBITION arrows along the curbs and 4" YELLOW lines on each side of the raised median.

View 1 (100' R/W, 80' roadway, 10' outside strips): A raised median 14' wide with a 1' offset on each side to the 4" yellow lines (dimensions 1', 14', 1') sits on the center line, with 40' of roadway on each side. Lane strings read 12', 10', 10' from curb to median on the lower side and 10', 22' on the upper side. The median ends with a reverse curve taper (NOTE 7) into a single left turn lane with arrow. At the intersection, a 4' dimension and a 1' dimension show the offsets at the median end, and lanes read 10', 10', 10' and 12' with 22' to the outer line.

View 2 (104' R/W, 80' roadway, 12' outside strips): Same 14' raised median with 1' offsets, 40' of roadway each side. The median ends in a rounded nose (NOTE 6 & 7 callout) and a left turn pocket opens with a 12' dimension at the taper, a left turn arrow, and a 6' wide chevron-hatched area drawn in the lane between the median end and the left turn lane. Intersection lane strings read 12', 10', 10' plus 22'.

View 3 (104' R/W, 80' roadway, 12' outside strips): A narrower raised median 8' wide with 1' offsets (1', 8', 1'), 40' of roadway each side. Lane strings read 24', 11', 8', 11', 11', 13'. The rounded nose end (NOTE 6) tapers with a reverse curve into a left turn lane with arrow. At the intersection, strings read 24', 11', 10', 11', 11', 13'. Below the views the text SEE SHEET 1 FOR NOTES appears. Title block: TYPICAL MAJOR HIGHWAY STRIPING TREATMENTS, Drawing No. S-401.0, sheet 3 of 5.
notes: SEE SHEET 1 FOR NOTES. The notes themselves are not on this sheet. Callouts refer to NOTE 7, NOTE 6 & 7 and NOTE 6 (median end treatment) on sheet 1. Other labels: 4" YELLOW (each side of every raised median), RAISED MEDIAN, STOPPING PROHIBITION.
title: Typical Major Highway Striping Treatments, Raised Median (Prior to 11-10-99), Sheet 3 of 5
summary: Three plan views of major highway raised median striping on 100-foot and 104-foot rights-of-way with an 80-foot roadway. Medians are 14' or 8' wide with 4-inch yellow lines on each side, and each ends at a signalized intersection with a left turn pocket, one with a 6' chevron-hatched area. Notes 6 and 7 on sheet 1 govern the median ends.

description:

A critical driveway with a 30' MIN. dimension is at the lower curb. On the right, the center turn lane ends with a reverse curve labeled 60' OR 80' into a left turn pocket with a left turn arrow, and the double yellow center line continues to the intersection. Intersection widths read 23' to 24', 11', 10' to 12', 11', 11' and 12' to 13'.

View 2, standard flare section: Same 126' R/W, 102' roadway (51' each side) at mid-block, with a 12' strip each side. The curb flares out to the 136' R/W and 112' roadway (56' each side of center, 136' overall) over a STANDARD FLARE SECTION. Two 150' dimensions are shown, with a CR=25' curb return at each corner. A 12' wide, 100' TO 120' TAPER marks the center turn lane transition into two left turn lanes (two left turn arrows). Intersection strings read 24', 11', 11', 10', 10', 11', 11', 13' with 56' per side and 136' overall.

notes: SEE SHEET 1 FOR NOTES. The notes themselves are not on this sheet. Callout on the sheet: NOTE 6 (raised median end). Other labels: CRITICAL DRIVEWAY, 30' MIN., 60' OR 80', 100' TO 120' TAPER, TAPER, CR=25', 150', STANDARD FLARE SECTION, 4" YELLOW, RAISED MEDIAN, STOPPING PROHIBITION.

title: Typical Major Highway Striping Treatments, Class II (104' R/W - 80' Roadway), Sheet 5 of 5

description:
Sheet 1 of 2 of Drawing S-401.1 (City of Los Angeles Department of Transportation), approved 11/18/1999 by Frances T. Banerjee, General Manager. A low-resolution scan, with some small dimension strings hard to read. Heading: SECONDARY HIGHWAYS (prior to 11-10-99), 86' R/W - 66' roadway (with 90' R/W - 70' roadway flare at intersection). Three stacked plan views, each running from mid-block on the left to a signalized intersection (circled S) on the right.

Top view, open-ended two-way left turn lane (2WLTL): 86' right-of-way, 66' roadway (33' each side of center), 10' outside strips. A double yellow center line with a center turn lane about 10' wide and outer lane strings of about 18' (partly [illegible]). A critical driveway at the lower curb has a 30' MIN. dimension. The center turn lane ends in a reverse curve labeled 60' OR 80' leading into a left turn pocket with a left turn arrow at the intersection.

Middle view, closed-ended 2WLTL: Same 86' R/W, 66' roadway (33' each side), 10' strips. A 12" YELLOW line marks the closed end, followed by a reverse curve labeled 60' OR 80' and a left turn arrow at the intersection. A critical driveway at the lower curb has a 70' MIN. dimension. At the intersection the roadway flares to 90' R/W and 70' roadway (35' each side), with 10' strips, and the curb return is marked R18. Below the view, dimension lines read TAPER 150', STANDARD FLARE SECTION 300' and STOPPING PROHIBITION, with 150' on each side of the intersection centerline. Lane strings are small and partly [illegible].

Bottom view, left turn pocket with flare: 86' R/W, 66' roadway (33' each side), 10' strips, with a 12" YELLOW line and a 100' to 120' taper ending in a 12' wide left turn lane (arrow). Below are dimension lines TAPER 150', 150', STANDARD FLARE SECTION 300' and STOPPING PROHIBITION. At the intersection the flare shows two left turn arrows and a 70' roadway (35' each side) with 90' R/W. Title block: TYPICAL SECONDARY HIGHWAY STRIPING TREATMENTS, Drawing No. S-401.1, sheet 1 of 2.
notes:
NOTES:
1. Selection of length of left turn pocket lane depends on demand, spacing between intersections and location of critical driveways to be served by two-way left turn lanes (2WLTL). The desirable length at signalized intersections is at least 40' of storage per vehicle per signal cycle averaged during the peak hour. However, this desirable length often may not be feasible. Minimum lengths at signalized intersections on highways with continuous median channelization are: 100' at major highways, 100' at secondary highways, 60' at collector streets, 40' at local streets. Minimum pocket lengths for secondary highways without continuous median channelization may be less, depending on turning volumes and parking impacts.
2. Utilize 60' reversals for posted speed limits of 35 mph and less, and 80' reversals for posted speed limits of 40 mph and greater. A 40' minimum (MIN.) reversal may be used in exceptional situations for critical driveways.
3. Selection of an open-ended (as shown in top drawing) versus closed-ended (as shown in middle drawing) 2WLTL is dependent, in part, on the proximity of a critical driveway to be served by a 2WLTL. Minimum distances to critical driveways are shown.
4. The painted reversal for a single left turn lane may be eliminated at a signalized intersection on a selective basis if spillover is recurrent and if it is not feasible to lengthen the left-turn pocket.
title: Typical Secondary Highway Striping Treatments (86' R/W - 66' Roadway, Prior to 11-10-99), Sheet 1 of 2

Notes set minimum left turn pocket lengths by street class (100', 100', 60', 40'), reversal lengths by speed, and when a painted reversal may be dropped.

description:
Sheet 1 of 3 of Drawing S-404.3, SHARED MOBILITY PARKING (SMP) ZONES ON-STREET AND SIDEWALK (City of Los Angeles Department of Transportation, approved 11/07/19 by Seleta J. Reynolds, General Manager). A low-resolution scan. Two plan views and a legend, all drawn not to scale.

Shared Mobility Parking: On-Street (plan view): Traffic runs left to right (DIRECTION OF VEHICULAR TRAVEL arrow). The face of curb and back of curb are the two lines at the bottom. A rectangular SMP zone is marked with a 4" WHITE (TYP.) outline, closed at the curb side by the curb. The zone is 11' MIN. to 19' MAX. long along the curb and 7' MIN. to 8' MAX. deep from the curb, with a 10' MIN. dimension from the curb up to the top of the dimension. Inside the zone, three 24" circular pavement symbols are placed in a row: bicycle, P, and scooter. Spacing along the zone from the left end reads 18" MIN., 24", 8" MIN., 24", 8" MIN., 24", 18" MIN. The symbols are centered in the 7' MIN.-8' MAX. depth, with equal (EQ.) spaces above and below. At each end of the zone next to the curb is a wheel stop (hatched rectangle, SEE NOTE 2) and a sign post. The left sign is labeled OM-3R and the right sign is labeled OM-3L. A solid circle (flexible bollard sign) is drawn at the right end corners of the zone and at the midpoint of the street-side line.

Shared Mobility Parking: Sidewalk (plan view): Traffic runs left to right. Face of curb and back of curb lines are at the top. A rectangular SMP zone with a 4" WHITE (TYP.) outline sits on the sidewalk below the curb. The zone is 8.5' MIN. long and 4' MIN. to 7.5' MAX. deep, with equal (EQ.) space above and below the symbols. Inside, the symbols from left to right are bicycle, P, and scooter, each 24". Spacing from the left end reads 6" MIN., 24", 8" MIN., 24", 8" MIN., 24", 6" MIN. A callout from the curb to the zone reads SEE NOTES 10 & 11.

Legend: a solid circle is FLEXIBLE BOLLARD SIGN, a solid half-round post symbol is SIGN POST, and a hatched rectangle is WHEEL STOP, RUBBERIZED (6"Wx48"Lx4"H).
notes: SEE NOTE 2 (wheel stop) and SEE NOTES 10 & 11 (sidewalk clearances) are referenced on this sheet. The notes are on sheet 3 of 3 of this drawing. Legend: flexible bollard sign, sign post, wheel stop rubberized (6" wide x 48" long x 4" high).

title: Shared Mobility Parking (SMP) Pavement Marking Symbols (Scooter, P, Bicycle), Sheet 2 of 3
summary: Stencil details for the three pavement symbols used in Shared Mobility Parking zones: a scooter, the letter P, and a bicycle. Each is a 24-inch diameter circle with stencil bridges, shown not to scale.

description: Sheet 3 of 3 of Drawing S-404.3, SHARED MOBILITY PARKING (SMP) ZONES ON-STREET AND SIDEWALK (City of Los Angeles Department of Transportation, approved 11/07/19 by Seleta J. Reynolds, General Manager). A text-only notes sheet in three groups: Shared Mobility Parking: On-Street (notes 1 to 8), Shared Mobility Parking: Sidewalk (notes 9 to 16), and Miscellaneous (note 17). The notes set minimum clearances for SMP zones from driveways, fire hydrants, crosswalks, curb ramps, stop and yield signs and traffic signals, and prohibit SMP zones in bus zones, peak hour lanes and restricted curb areas.
notes:
NOTES:
SHARED MOBILITY PARKING: ON-STREET
1. Parking meter heads, posts and signs shall be removed or adjusted as needed if shared mobility parking (SMP) is installed in a parking meter zone.
2. Rubberized wheel stops shall be used at the ends of the SMP zones if located next to on-street parking.
3. Minimum clearance from the top of driveway shall be 5'.
4. Minimum clearance from a fire hydrant shall be 15'.
5. SMP zones shall remain clear of bus zones.
6. SMP zones shall not be installed in peak hour lanes, red curb zones, or in parking restricted areas (i.e. tow-away no stopping any time "T.A.N.S.A.T.", no parking any time "N.P.A.T.", etc.).
7. Minimum clearance from two or more consecutive parking spaces shall be 5'.
8. SMP zones shall not be installed within 30' of a limit line at a traffic signal or within 25' of a "STOP" or "YIELD" sign.
SHARED MOBILITY PARKING: SIDEWALK
9. A minimum of 5' of unobstructed sidewalk must be maintained for a pedestrian pathway.
10. Where there is no parking on the adjacent street, provide:
   A. Minimum clearance of 1'-6" from the face of curb to the edge of the SMP zone.
11. Where there is parking on the adjacent street, provide:
   A. Minimum clearance of 3' from the face of curb to the edge of the SMP zone.
   B. Minimum clearance of 4' from the face of curb to the edge of the SMP zone if the adjacent parking is a loading zone or disabled parking space.
   C. Minimum clearance of 4' of unobstructed pathway at the ends of the SMP zone.
12. Minimum clearance of 5' from the marked crosswalk line or top of curb ramp.
13. Minimum clearance of 5' from the top of driveway.
14. Minimum clearance from a fire hydrant shall be 15'.
15. SMP zones shall remain clear of bus loading and unloading zones.
16. SMP zones shall not:
   A. Block access to building entrances or exits.
   B. Obstruct utility accesses such as manholes, pullboxes, street light poles, power poles, etc.
   C. Obstruct the use of sidewalk furniture such as benches, newsstands, mailboxes, bus shelters, etc.
MISCELLANEOUS
17. All pavement markings shall be skid-resistant.
title: Shared Mobility Parking (SMP) Zones On-Street and Sidewalk Notes, Sheet 3 of 3
summary: General notes for Shared Mobility Parking zones, grouped as on-street, sidewalk and miscellaneous. Zones need 5' from driveways, 15' from fire hydrants, 30' from a signal limit line and 25' from stop or yield signs. Sidewalk zones keep at least 5' of pedestrian path and 1'-6" to 4' from the face of curb depending on adjacent parking. All markings must be skid-resistant.

description: Sheet 2 of 2 of Drawing S-405.0, INTERSECTION STRIPING (City of Los Angeles Department of Transportation). A text-only sheet headed POLICY AND CRITERIA with three groups of numbered notes: GENERAL (1 to 3), MULTIPLE TURNS (4 to 9) and LONGITUDINAL STRIPING (10 to 11, with sub-items A to F). The scan carries pink highlighter marks over parts of notes 2, 3 and 11A to 11D, which do not change the text. The notes cover when dotted intersection striping (cat tracks) is used, cat track dimensions (4 inch wide, about 1 foot long, 7 feet center to center, per CA MUTCD Details 40 and 41), curve geometry for left and right turn cat tracks, lane offsets, crosswalk lengths at the receiving end, signal phasing where opposing multiple left turn cat tracks are close, and when longitudinal cat tracks are required.
notes:
POLICY AND CRITERIA
GENERAL
1. Dotted intersection striping, more commonly known as "cat tracks", shall be used for all multiple turns and under special conditions for longitudinal striping, as shown in Note 11.
2. Cat tracks are 4" in width and should be approximately one foot in length, 7' center to center (CA MUTCD Detail 40 and 41). They shall be the same color as the stripe they extend, except that cat tracks connecting to double yellow lines shall be 4" yellow.
3. Solid intersection striping should be installed for single or double right turns where one of the lanes is a trap lane (see S-491.0). Trap lanes shall be separated from adjacent through lanes by a longitudinal line.
MULTIPLE TURNS
4. The beginning-of-curve of cat tracks for left turns shall be tangent to the barrier line or its prolongation at or downstream of the interior crosswalk line. The end-of-curve shall be parallel to the receiving lane line or its prolongation at or upstream of the exterior crosswalk line and located as described in Note 8.
5. The beginning-of-curve of cat tracks for right turns should be at the radial extension of the beginning of the curb return and tangent to the barrier line. Where the curb lane width is sufficiently wide to allow a larger curve for the cat track than one beginning as described above, in order to provide an improved travel path, the beginning of curve may begin upstream of the BCR. When the barrier line at the beginning-of-curve is not parallel to the curb, the curve shall be tangent to the barrier line or its prolongation. The beginning of curve should be positioned to maintain a minimum width at the curb return equal to the approach width, or 12 feet, whichever is smaller. The portion of curve upstream of the exterior crosswalk line shall be a solid stripe. The end-of-curve shall be parallel to the receiving lane line and located as described in Note 8.
6. The cat track line may be offset 1 foot from the receiving lane line, to provide a wider reception width for the number one turn lane when: 1) the No. 1 receiving lane is less than 11 feet; and 2) the curb lane width (or the combined No. 2 and No. 3 lane widths) equals or exceeds 21 feet with parking, or 13 feet with parking prohibited. When the offset criteria are met, the reception width for the number one lane (lane width plus offset) should be 12 feet where possible and the dimension between the cat track and curb shall equal or exceed 20 feet with parking, or 12 feet with parking prohibited.
7. Intersection striping for multiple turns generally should direct motorists to non-curb lanes whenever possible, since they may be blocked by parked vehicles and the radius would be smaller than necessary.
8. For multiple left turns, where there is no raised median separating the opposing traffic on the receiving end, the crosswalk on the receiving end should be at least 20 feet and the double yellow center line through that crosswalk may be deleted. Where there is a median island, the crosswalk on the receiving end should be 15 feet.
9. Where the distance between cat tracks for multiple left-turns in opposite directions is less than 30 feet, lead-lag left-turn or opposed signal phasing shall be used.
LONGITUDINAL STRIPING
10. Wherever feasible, the need for longitudinal cat tracks should be avoided by designing travel paths through the intersection parallel to raised medians or curb lines.
11. Special conditions where longitudinal cat tracks within the intersection are required include:
   A. Where the offset in striping through the intersection is more than 2 feet.
   B. Where opposing left turn lanes are offset to the right of each other.
   C. Where the striping has a taper or a curve that begins within 50 feet of the approach to an intersection.
   D. Where a taper or curve ends within 20 feet of the intersection.
   E. Where the design speed associated with the radius of curvature of the travel path through the intersection equals or is less than the applicable speed limit.
   F. At intersections with sharp crest vertical curvature where the departure striping is not continuously visible to approaching motorists.
title: Intersection Striping, Policy and Criteria, Sheet 2 of 2
summary: Policy notes for intersection striping with cat tracks (dotted lines through intersections). Covers 4 inch by about 1 foot cat tracks at 7 feet center to center, curve geometry for multiple left and right turns, a 1 foot lane offset rule, receiving-end crosswalk lengths of 20 and 15 feet, lead-lag or opposed phasing when opposing left turn cat tracks are under 30 feet apart, and conditions that require longitudinal cat tracks.

description:
Drawing S-410.4.1, Parking Meter Post Installation, Dirt or Asphalt Setting (City of Los Angeles Department of Transportation, approved 12/03/2020 by Seleta J. Reynolds, General Manager, sheet 1 of 1).

Elevation: A vertical steel post with a reamed inside at the top (callout Reamed Inside of Top) stands in a concrete post footing set in dirt or asphalt next to a curb. The post is 42" overall. From the top of curb to the top of post is 30" (dimension From Top of Curb), and the post extends 12" below the top of curb. A 1/4" hole is drilled on one side only, 26" below the top of the post (Drill 1/4" Hole (One Side Only)). The post flange is set in cement grout at the top of the footing, with a shaped grout cap around the post at the surface. A 20" dimension runs from the post to the curb face. Curb section at right: Top of Curb, Curb Face (near vertical, slightly sloped) and Gutter are labeled. The concrete post footing is 8" MIN. square or round, extends 18" MIN. below the top of curb, and the post bottom is 6" MIN. above the footing bottom. Callout: Concrete Post Footing.

Specification for post and notes appear at the lower left.
notes:
SPECIFICATION FOR POST
Steel pipe, standard weight, 2" x 42" long, ASTM-A120-63T, new and unused, hot dipped galvanized, top reamed.
NOTES
1. Concrete to be Class 560-C-3250.
2. Post to be level straight.
3. Area to be left clean.
4. Cement grout - 1 (cement) : 2 1/2 (sand).
title: Parking Meter Post Installation, Dirt or Asphalt Setting
summary: Elevation of a 2 inch by 42 inch galvanized steel parking meter post set in an 8 inch minimum square or round concrete footing, 18 inches minimum deep, 20 inches back from the curb face. The post top stands 30 inches above the top of curb and has a 1/4 inch hole drilled one side only 26 inches below the top.

description:
Drawing S-410.4.2, Parking Meter Post Installation, Concrete Setting (City of Los Angeles Department of Transportation, approved 12/03/2020 by Seleta J. Reynolds, General Manager, sheet 1 of 1).

Elevation: A vertical steel post, top reamed on the inside (Reamed Inside of Top), is set through a hole cut in a concrete sidewalk next to a curb. The post is 42" overall, with 30" above the sidewalk surface and 12" below it. A 1/4" diameter hole is drilled on one side only 26" below the post top. A 20" dimension runs from the post to the curb face. The sidewalk is labeled Concrete Sidewalk, with Finish Surface at its top, and the curb face and gutter at right. The post is placed in a 3 1/4" diameter hole cut in the sidewalk, filled with cement grout. The post flange is set in cement grout with a shaped grout cap at the surface, and wooden wedges 1" x 3/4" x 2" +/- long hold the post upright. Below the sidewalk the dirt is cleaned out (Clean out dirt under sidewalk approx. as shown) so the grout forms a flared plug wider than the hole. A 1" dimension is shown below the post bottom, and the 3 1/4" Dia. dimension is shown at the bottom of the grout.

Specification for post and notes appear at the lower left.
notes:
SPECIFICATION FOR POST
Steel pipe, standard weight, 2" x 42" long, ASTM-A120-63T, new and unused, hot dipped galvanized, top reamed.
NOTES
1. Post to be level straight.
2. Area to be left clean.
3. Cement grout - 1 (cement) : 2 1/2 (sand).

title: Parking Meter Post Installation, Concrete Setting

description:
Drawing S-410.4.3, Parking Meter Post Installation on Concrete Bridge (City of Los Angeles Department of Transportation, approved 12/03/2020 by Seleta J. Reynolds, General Manager, sheet 1 of 1).

Elevation: A 30" long steel post with reamed inside top stands on a post flange base bolted to a concrete sidewalk (bridge deck) next to a curb. The post rises 30" above the sidewalk surface, with a 1/4" hole drilled on one side only 26" below the post top. A 20" dimension runs from the post to the curb face. The flange base is set in cement grout and fastened by 4 stud bolt anchors. Concrete Sidewalk, Top of Curb, Curb Face and Gutter are labeled. Callout: 4 - 1/2" holes to be drilled 1 7/8" deep to receive 4 stud bolt anchors, 1/2" x 3" nuts to be steel hex galvanized, 1/2" washers to be flat steel galvanized. Washers may be used under base as shims for leveling. 30" unthreaded post welded onto the flange.

Detail: Post Flange Base (plan and side view): The base is a 6" square, 1/4" hot roll steel plate with 4 chamfered corners (7/8" dimension at a chamfer) and four 3/4" drill holes, each 1" from two adjacent plate edges. A 1/2" drill hole is at the center, and the post is attached with a continuous weld around its circumference. The side view shows the 1/4" plate with the post welded to it.

Specification for post and grout notes appear at the lower left.
notes:
4 - 1/2" holes to be drilled 1 7/8" deep to receive 4 stud bolt anchors. 1/2" x 3" nuts to be steel hex galvanized. 1/2" washers to be flat steel galvanized. Washers may be used under base as shims for leveling. 30" unthreaded post welded onto the flange.
SPECIFICATION FOR POST
Steel pipe, standard weight, 2" x 30" long, ASTM-A120-63T, new and unused, hot dipped galvanized, top reamed.
Cement grout - 1 (cement) : 2 1/2 (sand).
Detail labels: 3/4" drill, 4 holes. Continuous weld. 1/2" drill. 1/4" hot roll steel plate.
title: Parking Meter Post Installation on Concrete Bridge

The plate is anchored to a concrete bridge deck with four 1/2 inch stud bolts in holes drilled 1 7/8 inches deep, and set in cement grout 20 inches from the curb face.

Sheet 2 of 7 of Drawing S-414.4, LEFT TURN AND MEDIAN CHANNELIZATION PAVEMENT MARKINGS (City of Los Angeles Department of Transportation). Five plan views, Cases 5 to 9, each a short stretch of a roadway (curb lines in bold, lane lines dashed, center striping double yellow) with an intersection or driveway. Each case is drawn not to scale, with R1-1 STOP sign symbols at stop-controlled side streets. Left turn arrows mark the pocket lanes. A STOP sign (R1-1) graphic is also shown near the center of the sheet.

Case 5: A roadway running left to right ends in a signalized driveway-type intersection (circled S) with a DRIVEWAY box above and a critical driveway box below on the near side. The left turn pocket on the near approach is entered by a 12" YELLOW taper (reversal with diagonal hatch) and a left turn arrow, with NOTE 5 at the pocket. On the far side the pocket is mirrored with a left turn arrow and a 12" YELLOW taper. A text label MAJOR OR STREET TYPE DRIVEWAY identifies the cross street type.

Case 6: An intersection with an R1-1 stop-controlled side street. On the near approach the double yellow center line continues with a left turn lane (arrow) without a reversal taper, with NOTE 6 at the center line. On the far side the left turn lane closes with a 12" YELLOW taper and diagonal hatch, with NOTE 7.

Case 7: A roadway section with NO DRIVEWAYS on either side. A painted median with a double yellow center line closes into a 12" YELLOW tapered, diagonal-hatched end (NOTE 8). A 200' dimension runs from the taper end to a MINOR DRIVEWAY on the far side, with another MINOR DRIVEWAY on the upper curb.

Case 8: A roadway with a double yellow painted median past two MINOR DRIVEWAY boxes, then a stop-controlled side street (R1-1) entering from below. On the far side of the side street a left turn pocket with an arrow opens with a 12" YELLOW taper.

Case 9: A roadway with a double yellow two-way left turn lane (NOTE 9) running continuously across a stop-controlled side street (R1-1 at both corners) and a CRITICAL DRIVEWAY box on the far upper curb. Title block: LEFT TURN AND MEDIAN CHANNELIZATION PAVEMENT MARKINGS, Drawing No. S-414.4, sheet 2 of 7.

description: Sheet 7 of 7 of Drawing S-414.4, LEFT TURN AND MEDIAN CHANNELIZATION PAVEMENT MARKINGS (City of Los Angeles Department of Transportation). A text-only sheet giving 25 numbered notes that apply to Cases 1 to 25 on sheets 1 to 6. The notes cover channelization for advance left turn lanes (S-491.0), when reversals may be deleted, minimum lengths of two-way left turn lanes (2WLTL), pockets, reversals and side-by-side left turn lanes, use of painted medians, taper separations, shadow widths and curb lane widths at red curb.
notes:
Notes
1. Refer to S-491.0 for channelization associated with advance left-turn lanes.
2. Refer to S-401.0 Notes 1-5 regarding left turn lane details on the approach to signalized intersections.
3. At a signalized approach the reversal may be deleted and the double yellow line extended as shown only if: 1) the minimum length of the left turn lane is provided per S-401.0; 2) spillover is recurrent; 3) there is a 2WLTL upstream of the left-turn; or 4) an operational decision has been made to provide left-turn storage into a critical driveway.
4. A 2WLTL may be installed adjacent to an advance left turn lane (serving only the through move along the adjacent reach) but shall not be installed adjacent to a unidirectional left turn lane.
5. Signalized driveways should be served with a left-turn pocket lane. Where the driveway within the intersection is not signalized, a 2WLTL may be considered.
6. The reversal of a striped left-turn lane may be deleted at an unsignalized intersection. Where additional storage is desired the lane should be lengthened or replaced by a 2WLTL.
7. The 2WLTL may be extended and the curved median closure (cigar nose) eliminated where it is desired to provide a refuge for vehicles turning left from a driveway or street.
8. A painted median should be striped where the nearest driveway is more than 200 feet away or where it is not desired to provide U-turn capability for motorists to park at the curb.
9. A 2WLTL may be used instead of a left-turn pocket lane where an operational decision has been made to provide left-turn storage into a critical driveway, or where it is desired to provide refuge for vehicles turning left from a driveway or street.
10. The absolute minimum length of a 2WLTL under constrained conditions is 30 feet (6 feet of interior stripe, 18 feet of gap and 6 feet of interior stripe).
11. This is an option to Case 10 where there are no driveways.
12. For interior distances less than 30 feet install at least 7 feet of lane line striping and a diagonal double yellow stripe for guidance.
13. The absolute minimum length for a left-turn lane reversal is 40 feet. Thus, the minimum length for back-to-back left-turn lanes is 70 feet (15 feet of storage, 40 feet of reversal and 15 feet of storage).
14. Use to maximize 2WLTL storage or where the striping of the 30 foot minimum length of a 2WLTL is not possible between the offset cross streets and it is desired to provide 2WLTL storage at the cross streets.
15. Case 16 striping may be used if an operation decision has been made to maximize left turn storage for one of the legs of a jogged intersection, while on the other hand sacrificing left turn storage for the other leg. The minimum length of the left turn pocket is 15 feet. Consideration should be given to prohibiting left turns from the leg without a pocket.
16. The minimum width for each side-by-side left-turn lane is 9 feet and the minimum length is 15 feet.
17. The 8 inch white diagonal line is reserved for jogged intersections with minor offsets where the opposing left turn paths do not overlap. Assume a single radius for each vehicular path.
18. Use Case 19 to provide storage into a critical driveway as discussed in S-401.0, Note 4.
19. The tapered double yellow line may be partially or completely deleted where it is desired to accommodate left-turns to or from a driveway within the reach of the taper.
20. One of the tapered double yellow lines may be broken where it is desired to accommodate left turns to or from a driveway within the reach of the taper.
21. Tapers in different directions shall be separated by a 50 feet minimum tangent parallel to the edge of roadway. Adjacent tapers in the same direction should be avoided and replaced by a longer single taper, curve or curve-tangent-curve.
22. All left turn lanes are to be shadowed from opposing traffic with a left-turn lane or (painted or raised) median on the opposite leg. The minimum width of shadow at the receptive center line is 9 feet, unless a protected left turn phase is provided.
23. When the tapered double yellow line is deleted as per Note 20 an 18 feet minimum curb lane width to the unstriped taper shall be provided where curb stopping is allowed.
24. A through pavement marking arrow should be provided where a single through lane lies adjacent to left-turn and right-turn lanes.
25. Striping may be extended across an unsignalized intersection where it is desired to provide continuous storage on the approach to a signalized intersection downstream. Consideration should be given to prohibiting lefts into and out of the cross street.
title: Left Turn and Median Channelization Pavement Markings, Notes 1 to 25, Sheet 7 of 7
summary: The 25 general notes for the left turn and median channelization cases on S-414.4. They set minimum lengths of 30 feet for a 2WLTL, 40 feet for a reversal, 70 feet for back-to-back pockets and 15 feet for a pocket, 9 foot minimum side-by-side lane and shadow widths, 50 feet between opposing tapers and 18 feet of curb lane beside red curb. They also say when reversals, tapers and cigar nose closures may be deleted.
